title: Next: Ground Loop
summary: Closing splash turns successful transparency into a synchronization problem: visible records are not enough if messages, clocks and physical routes do not stay aligned.
panelPlan: Full-page closing splash at a municipal truck-fill yard after a long day. Use two physical ledgers or route boards, rugged radios, clocks and trucks as ordinary infrastructure rather than symbols.
Let the composition contain small timing disagreements—different clock faces or paper timestamps—without showing the duplicate dispatch that opens Issue 6.
Keep all equipment functioning. The threat is latency and mismatch, not catastrophe. Do not show the pump-start electrical failure, hydro gallery, relay redesign or any later Ground Loop solution.
Set IF PUBLIC SKY ONLY WORKS WHEN COMMUNICATIONS ARE CLEAN, IT DOES NOT WORK as the hard closing premise above NEXT: GROUND LOOP.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now everyone can see the ledgers.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Everyone can see who got protected first.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It did not change the desert.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A message can still be late.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A relay can still go silent.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Two honest copies of the truth can still arrive hours apart.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: If Public Sky only works when communications are clean, it does not work.

directionInline.text: Non-diegetic closing teaser. Preserve exact caption text. The page may evoke delay and imperfect synchronization but must not depict the exact duplicate-truck mistake, motor-noise failure, seized cabinet, physical relay workaround or other Issue 6 event.
